models_evaluated: convolutional neural network with differential privacy-enhanced domain transfer (DP-DT)
convolutional neural network with non-DP domain transfer

links.outcome: AUC drop from single-institution to cross-institution performance across five chest radiograph datasets
links.effect: Cross-institutional AUC decreased by 0.07 (VinDr-CXR), 0.07 (ChestX-ray14), 0.07 (CheXpert), 0.18 (UKA-CXR), and 0.07 (PadChest) for DP-DT, with similar drops for non-DP models.
links.quote: Even with high privacy levels (ε ≈ 1), DP-DT showed no evidence of differences compared with non–DP-DT in terms of a decrease in AUC of cross-institutional performance as compared with single-institutional performance (VinDr-CXR: 0.07 vs 0.07, P = .96; ChestX-ray14: 0.07 vs 0.06, P = .12; CheXpert: 0.07 vs 0.07, P = .18; UKA-CXR: 0.18 vs 0.18, P = .90; and PadChest: 0.07 vs 0.07, P = .35).

links.outcome: Effect of differential privacy on cross-institutional diagnostic AUC and subgroup performance versus non-DP models
links.effect: At ε≈1, no evidence of AUC differences between DP-DT and non-DP-DT; subgroup AUC differences under 1% for sex subgroups and nearly all age subgroups. Privacy protection itself was not measured.
links.quote: Cross-institutional performance of artificial intelligence models was not affected by DP.

unlisted_practices: Differential privacy-enhanced domain transfer for privacy-preserving collaborative model training across institutions

screen.reason: Empirically tests whether applying differential privacy (DP) during domain transfer across multi-institutional chest radiograph datasets impacts diagnostic performance and demographic fairness.
